outcome: maternal complications (PPH, eclampsia, acute renal failure, HELLP syndrome, pulmonary edema, maternal deaths)
perinatal complications (low birth weight, fetal growth restriction, intrauterine fetal death, perinatal mortality)
cohort: 240 women with severe pre-eclampsia after 34 weeks of pregnancy, excluding those with multiple pregnancies, anemia, pre-existing hypertension, epilepsy, diabetes, or vascular/renal disease, at SKMCH, Muzaffarpur, Bihar, India.
finding: Severe pre-eclampsia was associated with increased maternal (1.66% incidence of complications) and perinatal complications (80% low birth weight, 20% fetal growth restriction, 5% intrauterine fetal death, and 12% perinatal mortality).
mod_finding: 56.6% of women with severe pre-eclampsia had vaginal births, while 43.5% had Cesarean sections, often due to failed induction or stalled labor.
birth_weight: Low birth weight in 80% of cases
